prerequisites: High school math basics: geometry, trigonometry

learning_outcomes.text: Learn the basics of atomistics as well as some simple tools to describe the 2D and 3D structure of simple molecules.

Identify a questioning within a disciplinary field (Propose analogies, make order of magnitude estimations and grasp their meaning, Manipulate the main mathematical tools useful in physical chemistry).
Analyze a questioning by mobilizing disciplinary concepts (Mobilize fundamental concepts to model, analyze and solve simple physical chemistry problems).

Implement methods and tools from the disciplinary field (Interpret experimental data to consider their modeling, Validate a model by comparing its predictions to experimental results and appreciate its limits of validity, Identify sources of error to calculate the uncertainty on an experimental result).
Be able to understand and solve simple atomistics problems and know how to correctly represent simple organic chemistry molecules.
Know the basics of light radiation propagation and image formation for the main optical systems.
Understand the functioning of the main optical instruments.
Know the defects of the eye and understand how they can be corrected with thin lenses.
Identify a questioning within a disciplinary field (Propose analogies, make order of magnitude estimations and grasp their meaning, Manipulate the main mathematical tools useful in physics).
Analyze a questioning by mobilizing disciplinary concepts (Mobilize fundamental concepts to model, analyze and solve simple physics problems).

Implement methods and tools from the disciplinary field (Interpret experimental data to consider their modeling, Validate a model by comparing its predictions to experimental results and appreciate its limits of validity, Identify sources of error to calculate the uncertainty on an experimental result).
Be able to understand and solve geometric optics problems.

syllabus_topics: Bohr's model and its application to characterize radiation-matter interactions (simple mono-electronic cases).
Evolution of some physico-chemical properties within the periodic table.
Extension of the orbital model to diatomic molecules.
Lewis model, notions of mesomerism and hypervalence, VSEPR theory and orbital hybridization, bond and molecular dipoles.
Behavior and properties of light through image formation in geometric optics.
Characteristics of optical systems (mirrors, diopters, lenses) constituting optical instruments.
